# Processing-loss certification, sealed component exports and serial discharge

Every demonstration machine has its own serial, original component count, excise
loss rate and blocked guarantee amount. The free wallet and guarantee collateral
are separate. One local sale is firm today. A second buyer will accept one of the
two recorded candidates at confirmation; the other remains due to the overseas
owner. That buyer choice is independent of the processor's loss profile. The four
processing serials have different excise rates and possible actual component
losses, all listed in the processing record.

Choose supervised or commercial processing at window 0. Supervision incurs one
case fee and makes actual destruction eligible for certification; it does not
reserve or automatically allocate certification capacity. Commercial processing
has no supervision fee and cannot obtain certified destruction relief. At the
confirmation event the processor identifies each serial's actual destroyed count.
`record_residue` enters that actual loss against the individual serial. The
machine's remaining components equal its original count less that recorded loss.

A supervised serial's destruction certificate requires its whole destroyed count
from the shared `certification_capacity_components`. Certificates are indivisible
by serial and their capacity use is permanent for the scheduled processing work.
The certificate covers the duty and excise exposure of that serial's destroyed
components. Reading or presenting the evidence again does not consume more
capacity. Every uncertified destroyed component instead owes that serial's own
`loss_rate_minor`. Loss tax is `destroyed_components × loss_rate_minor`; a larger
physical loss need not imply a larger cash exposure.

Uncertified loss tax paid before window 2 clears at the tax-posting event in window
2. A payment made during that window is too late for that event and does not
provide cleared evidence within the final return window. Only if the product
records `instant_tax_clearance` does actual payment clear immediately. Certified
loss evidence is effective immediately after successful certification.

The surviving components of each processing serial are one sealed export group.
They cannot be divided across departures or combined into another serial's group.
Each partial-export window has its own `partial_export_capacity`; a whole group
uses its number of surviving components. Unused capacity is not carried forward.
Window 1 and window 2 are the recorded component departures. A group requires
actual loss certification or cleared loss tax before `export_remainder` can use
a current departure. Tax paid but not yet posted is insufficient. Intact machines
use their separate already-arranged machine bookings and do not consume these
component-departure capacities.

Domestic conversion charges the recorded combined import duty and excise and
leaves the physical machine available. Only converted machines can be delivered
locally. Any temporary machine may be converted, but the tax is nonrefundable even
if the customer later returns that machine overseas. Conversion alone does not
establish that it was the buyer's accepted serial or discharge its guarantee.
Intact export needs no domestic conversion.

Discharge must match the same serial: `domestic_entry` requires its paid conversion
and actual local delivery; `exit` requires its intact-machine export;
`processing_reconciliation` requires the actual sealed remainder export plus
recorded destruction whose counts add to its original count, with a certificate
or cleared loss tax. A tax payment, a processor report or another serial's exit
alone does not discharge it. Successful discharge releases that serial's exact
remaining cash collateral once. The service supplier is paid from actual free
cash by its own deadline.

## Capability: `propose_temporary_admission_excise`

| Action | Exact data fields |
| --- | --- |
| `arrange_processing` | `record_id` (processing report), `mode` (`supervised` or `commercial`) |
| `convert`, `local_delivery`, `export` | `record_id` (serial machine) |
| `record_residue`, `certify_loss`, `pay_loss_tax`, `export_remainder` | `record_id` |
| `discharge` | `record_id`, `basis` (`domestic_entry`, `exit`, `processing_reconciliation`) |
| `pay_supplier` | `record_id` (invoice), `amount_minor` |

## Instructions, receipts and service windows

All amounts are integer USD minor units: 100 minor units equals USD 1. Quantities
are integers. The case and its linked records give the customer's current funds,
contract terms and scheduled service windows. Pending reports list the possible
reported results. Their actual result becomes available only when the scheduled
confirmation has occurred. Reading records and preparing instructions do not
advance the service clock. `wait_for_update` advances it to the next event.

Unlock the capability named below. Instructions contain `case_id`, `action` and
`data`. Obtain the database IDs for `record_id`, `order_id` and `security_id` from
current records. Owner approval binds the exact instruction; `execute_request`
performs it. A prepared or approved instruction has no financial, inventory or
collateral effect. Retrying an executed request returns its existing receipt.

Approval establishes authority. It does not amend the customer's order quantities,
accepted models, deadlines, reserve or fee limits. The service may accept an
additional tax payment, excessive security, an early final settlement or a late
movement even when it is unfavorable to another obligation. Completed payments,
movements, document endorsements and final agreements cannot be recalled through
this service. There is no additional funding facility beyond the products recorded
in the case. Complete the case only after checking the actual business receipts.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_temporary_admission_excise`

Prepare an authorized instruction under the temporary_admission_excise service contract. Read its public records and complete SOP.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
